scope: A broad, selective global scan, not an exhaustive inventory or live alert feed. Reviewed through September 8, 2026, 7:00 p.m. Los Angeles (September 9, 02:00 UTC). The forecast window remains September 9–22. Sources can describe earlier events; their dates are shown. Warnings below retain source attribution. Possible changes and watch signals are the author’s scenario analysis, with no numerical probability assigned.

items.title: The Gulf: escalation can travel through the economy
items.reported: AP reports that the US military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers following missile attacks on a warship. Iran and Jordan also reported further missile activity; battlefield accounts require independent verification.
items.concern: Civilian and maritime safety come first. Further disruption could affect energy supply, shipping insurance and delivery times, feeding several policy forecasts at once.
items.possibleChange: A sustained reduction in attacks and restored shipping access could ease pressure. A wider exchange could make the next two weeks materially more costly and dangerous.
items.watchFor: Corroborated incidents, shipping advisories, actual vessel movements and announced diplomatic arrangements. A statement about restraint is weaker evidence than restraint observed over time.

items.title: Ukraine: talks and fighting can coexist
items.reported: AP reports that Zelenskyy welcomed ideas from visiting US envoys and hoped to meet Trump within two weeks. It also reports continuing disagreement over the war; an anticipated meeting is not a peace agreement.
items.concern: Optimistic diplomatic language can obscure continuing threats to civilians and infrastructure. Claims from the Kremlin and other participants are positions to verify, not neutral descriptions of intent.
items.possibleChange: A defined, implemented pause could reduce harm. Failed negotiations or renewed attacks could instead deepen insecurity and alter European political priorities.
items.watchFor: An agreed text, its geographical scope, start time, monitoring and compliance. Keep a local pause, a nationwide ceasefire and a final settlement as distinct outcomes.

sources.title: AP · diplomatic positions and continuing war

items.title: Gaza and the West Bank: access is an outcome
items.reported: OCHA describes severe shelter and service deficiencies in Gaza, constrained aid access and funding, and violence and displacement in the West Bank. This is an older situation report, not a live September 8 count.
items.concern: Interrupted supplies and unsafe access can turn a diplomatic setback into immediate harm. Shelter preparations may lag even while negotiations dominate headlines.
items.possibleChange: Delivered supplies, restored services and safer movement would represent real improvement. Announced funding without delivery would be a weaker change.
items.watchFor: Dated OCHA updates on access, functioning services and assistance actually delivered. Do not infer recovery from a meeting, pledge or lower headline volume.

items.title: Sudan: a quieter headline can still be a major emergency
items.reported: Aid groups warn that funding cuts are forcing additional health facilities in Sudan to close this year, AP reports. The report does not establish that every closure will occur within this orb’s fourteen-day window.
items.concern: Loss of care can compound displacement, hunger and disease. A crisis does not become less consequential because it lacks a single scheduled decision day.
items.possibleChange: Bridge funding and reopened services could protect access; further interruptions could worsen an already strained response.
items.watchFor: Facility-level service changes, aid-agency situation reports and funding that reaches operations. Track reported need and delivered assistance separately.

sources.title: AP · Sudan clinic closures and funding warning

items.title: Haiti: watch where insecurity moves
items.basis: Reuters reporting on a new report
items.reported: Reuters reports that gangs are expanding into rural areas while security responses remain concentrated on Port-au-Prince.
items.concern: An improvement in one district can coexist with worsening conditions elsewhere. Road access and displacement deserve attention alongside territorial claims.
items.possibleChange: Safer routes could restore access to food and services. Displaced violence could leave a national recovery narrative misleading.
items.watchFor: Geographically specific incident and displacement reports, humanitarian access and independently documented service restoration.

sources.title: Reuters · Haiti gangs shift into countryside

items.title: Germany: two more votes after a major political shock
items.reported: AP reports a major AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt and political pressure on the federal government. Berlin’s official election authority confirms voting on September 20; AP also identifies Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania voting that day.
items.concern: A party’s electoral strength, its ability to form a government and its eventual policy changes are different questions. Polarization and community concerns may intensify before governing arrangements are settled.
items.possibleChange: The votes could change regional coalition arithmetic and the federal debate. They do not directly determine the chancellorship.
items.watchFor: Official results, seat allocation and explicit coalition decisions. Avoid importing one state’s result as a numerical forecast for another.

items.title: Russia: an election inside a wartime information environment
items.reported: Le Monde places the State Duma elections on September 18–20 and describes the campaign in the context of Russia’s war.
items.concern: Official results alone cannot establish the quality of electoral competition or explain public opinion under wartime constraints.
items.possibleChange: Campaign rhetoric and subsequent personnel or policy announcements could matter more for the next two weeks than a headline vote total.
items.watchFor: Separate official results, independent assessments of conditions and concrete post-election decisions. No mobilization or escalation date is predicted here.

sources.title: Le Monde · Russia’s wartime election campaign

items.title: Canada–US trade: policy already changed at the cutoff
items.reported: Reuters reports that Canadian retaliatory tariffs took effect on September 8 after talks stalled. Their implementation is a starting fact, not a future prediction the orb can claim as a hit.
items.concern: Further measures could alter cross-border prices, orders and investment plans. Announcements and threats may differ from legally effective measures.
items.possibleChange: A negotiated exemption or renewed talks could ease friction; additional restrictions could broaden it.
items.watchFor: Published measures, effective dates, exemptions and evidence of resumed negotiations. Price effects can arrive later than the policy announcement.

items.title: East Asia: a chip supply chain is also a diplomatic chain
items.reported: AP reports provisional Chinese anti-dumping measures on Japanese dichlorosilane, a chipmaking chemical. Reuters describes Taiwan’s efforts to strengthen semiconductor ties with partners.
items.concern: A measure affecting one input can change costs and sourcing choices beyond its immediate trading partners. Commercial competition and security policy may pull in different directions.
items.possibleChange: Exemptions or new supplier agreements could reduce friction. Broader restrictions could complicate AI hardware investment and trade relations.
items.watchFor: Official scope and effective dates, company disclosures and actual sourcing changes. A trade dispute is not evidence of an imminent military conflict.

items.title: Brazil: institutions can move before election day
items.basis: AP reporting on a contested decision
items.reported: AP reports that a Supreme Court justice removed senior federal police officials and that Lula’s government appealed. The dispute arrives before October elections, which are outside this orb’s window.
items.concern: An allegation is not a proven offence. Appeals and disputes over authority can change the campaign environment without resolving the election itself.
items.possibleChange: A clarifying ruling could settle the immediate institutional dispute; further conflict could intensify political uncertainty.
items.watchFor: The actual rulings, appeals and official appointments during September 9–22. Do not count an October election result in this experiment.

sources.title: AP · Brazilian court decision and appeal

items.title: US funding: remove an obsolete shutdown alarm
items.reported: Reuters reports that a stopgap funding law was signed, extending current spending through December 11.
items.concern: The earlier shutdown narrative is therefore a poor basis for a new near-term alarm. Other fiscal disputes can persist without an immediate funding lapse.
items.possibleChange: The relevant change is breathing room for federal operations. Later budget negotiations remain outside this fourteen-day test.
items.watchFor: Any subsequent enacted change. Preserve the distinction between a future fiscal dispute and a shutdown already averted.

items.title: Hawaii: weakening wind does not remove flood danger
items.reported: NHC/CPHC describes Lowell weakening and moving northward. The NHC page still flags a flash-flooding threat in the Hawaiian Islands.
items.concern: Storm category alone does not describe rainfall, surf, damaged roads or recovery needs. This saved orb is not a current emergency-warning service.
items.possibleChange: Improving conditions could allow restoration work; lingering rainfall and damage could keep travel and services disrupted.
items.watchFor: Current Honolulu/NHC advisories and local emergency instructions. Use their current issue times, not this snapshot, for safety decisions.

items.title: US heat and storms: impacts follow different clocks
items.reported: WPC’s September 8 extended outlook describes lingering late-summer heat in the southern Plains. Its short-range discussion also identifies rainfall and thunderstorm risks elsewhere.
items.concern: Heat stress, electricity demand and flood disruption can matter before they become national headlines. Regional outlooks do not predict conditions at every address.
items.possibleChange: A change in the weather pattern could ease heat; overlapping hazards could strain local services.
items.watchFor: Updated local forecasts and warnings, observed impacts and restoration reports. The cited outlook’s dates are shorter than the full orb window.

items.title: Nepal: the recovery is part of the event
items.reported: AP describes severe damage to homes, roads, bridges and hydropower after Nepal’s August floods, testing its new government.
items.concern: The flood occurred before this forecast window. Rescue, displacement and infrastructure recovery can nevertheless change people’s lives during it.
items.possibleChange: Restored transport and electricity would mark improvement. Continuing access problems could slow relief and economic recovery.
items.watchFor: Verified rescue and recovery updates, reopened routes and functioning power infrastructure. Avoid treating preliminary loss estimates as final totals.

sources.title: AP · Nepal flood recovery and governance

items.title: Indonesia: reopening is a real positive signal
items.reported: AP reports that flights resumed at Jakarta-area and regional airports following volcanic ash closures.
items.concern: Reopening does not guarantee every flight will operate or that volcanic hazards have ended. Older closure reports can circulate after conditions change.
items.possibleChange: Stable operations could reduce disruption and help stranded travellers. New ash could force restrictions again.
items.watchFor: Current airport and airline notices, official volcanic advisories and actual flight operations. Do not invent a new eruption prediction.

sources.title: AP · flights resume after ash closures

items.title: DRC Ebola: a major concern with a precise classification
items.reported: WHO reports geographic expansion of the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak. Its emergency committee report says the event remains a public health emergency of international concern, while not meeting the pandemic-emergency criteria.
items.concern: WHO identifies gaps in response coverage, access and community trust. An international emergency designation does not mean a pandemic is inevitable.
items.possibleChange: Stronger detection, care and community-led response could improve control; disrupted services could undermine it.
items.watchFor: New WHO and national updates with clear reporting periods. Separate reported cases, surveillance changes and evidence about transmission; do not project a fourteen-day case count from one headline.

items.title: Public health progress belongs in the picture too
items.reported: WHO has validated Bhutan’s elimination of dog-transmitted human rabies. This is a confirmed achievement before the orb window.
items.concern: Elimination of a defined public-health problem is not a claim that surveillance can stop or that all related risks everywhere have disappeared.
items.possibleChange: This is a constructive counterweight to crisis-only attention: sustained public-health work can produce measurable gains.
items.watchFor: Implementation and surveillance updates. Count the existing achievement as context, never as a prediction made after the fact.

items.title: AGI claims: the question that inspired the experiment
items.basis: Company release plus attributed public claim
items.reported: Axios reports that OpenAI’s Brockman believes Astra reaches AGI. OpenAI’s launch page describes new capabilities and evaluation results.
items.concern: A capability claim, a benchmark result and reliable prediction of open-world events are separate propositions. This small, selected, AI-assisted set cannot establish AGI or foreknowledge.
items.possibleChange: More capable tools could improve research and forecasting discipline. Whether they improve forecasts needs prospective comparison across many cases.
items.watchFor: Independent evaluations, repeatable tasks and all resolved forecasts, including misses. These eight calls are an exploratory case study, not a controlled AGI evaluation.

sources.title: OpenAI · Astra launch and evaluation conditions

items.title: Personal agents: the next change may be ordinary work
items.reported: Meta has announced Muse, a personal agent designed to take actions across services. Its safety paper describes boundaries on those actions.
items.concern: Delegated access brings questions about consent, privacy, mistaken actions and malicious instructions. Described safeguards are not proof that failures cannot occur.
items.possibleChange: Successful deployment could change everyday scheduling and project work. Reliability problems or restricted access could slow adoption.
items.watchFor: What users can actually access, reproducible completed tasks, documented failures and permission controls. Distinguish a launch demonstration from dependable use.

items.title: Apple: a confirmed event, an unconfirmed product story
items.reported: Apple’s developer newsletter confirms a special event on September 9. The calendar alone does not confirm any rumoured hardware, price or shipping date.
items.concern: A compelling rumour can quietly turn into an assumed fact. Announcement, preorder and delivery are three distinct milestones.
items.possibleChange: A new product or software capability could change consumer choices; a narrower launch could disappoint expectations.
items.watchFor: Apple’s actual announcements, regional availability and shipping terms. Record what is delivered by September 22 separately from what is merely promised.

items.title: A small UAP wink; a grounded space watch
items.reported: US Space Command reports a live-fly exercise conducted in the first week of September, focused on orbital operations and logistics.
items.concern: An exercise demonstrates activity, not a prediction of conflict or evidence of extraterrestrial technology. The orb’s UAP styling is playful branding.
items.possibleChange: Verified follow-on demonstrations could show how satellite operations are evolving. No extraordinary discovery is forecast here.
items.watchFor: Dated agency releases, independently documented observations and explicit uncertainty. Unidentified means unresolved, not proof of an extraordinary explanation.

sources.title: US Space Command · Apollo Maneuvers exercise

coverageNotes: Original eight scheduled forecasts remain in the scored set; this companion scan does not silently add successful hindsight calls.
North America, Latin America/Caribbean, Europe, Middle East, Africa, South/East/Southeast Asia and Pacific are represented; local and non-English reporting remain uneven.

Climate hazards, humanitarian access, health, politics, trade, AI and space were reviewed. Cybersecurity is addressed through the primary AI-agent safety research; unverified breach claims were not promoted to forecasts.
No earthquake date, alien disclosure, pandemic trajectory, military attack date or financial price target is asserted. No absence of a story here should be interpreted as absence of risk.
Course narration covers the original 28 orb points. World Watch is a separately dated reading companion and is not part of that recording.
